$comment: NBA 2K27 CAP BREAKERS.
This file was rewritten once real builder data arrived, because the previous model was wrong in
KIND, not just in its numbers. It assumed a small pool of breakers each worth a flat +1, capped at
two per attribute. The actual system, read off the NBA 2K HQ app's Cap Breaker page:
- Every attribute has FIVE cap breaker slots, not four in total.
- Each slot is worth a DIFFERENT, PER-ATTRIBUTE amount. Steal's first slot on the transcribed
build is +7; Close Shot's is +1.
- Gains DIMINISH down the slots. Block runs +6 / +5 / +4 / +3 / +2.
- Slots can be LOCKED. Mid-Range, Three-Point, Ball Handle, Speed With Ball, Defensive Rebound,
Speed and Agility have all five locked on the transcribed build, so no cap breaker can ever
raise them. `null` in a slot array means locked.
So a cap breaker is not a generic +1 you place wherever you like. It is a lookup: this body, this
attribute, this slot number, this many points. That makes the table below the whole model, and the
engine does nothing but read it.
APPARENT PATTERN, recorded as an observation and NOT relied on anywhere in code: attributes already
near this frame's ceiling are locked out (Mid-Range 94, Three-Point 91, Defensive Rebound 80, Speed
79, Agility 73) while low ones get large first-slot gains (Steal 60 -> +7, Free Throw 71 -> +6).
That suggests breakers push toward some per-attribute ceiling rather than granting a flat bonus.
One build is not enough to confirm it, so nothing is extrapolated from it — a body with no table
entry gets NO cap breaker plan at all rather than a guessed one.
HOW TO ADD A BODY: open the build in the NBA 2K HQ app, go to Cap Breakers, and transcribe each
row as `"<attribute_id>": { "slots": [s1, s2, s3, s4, s5], "newCap": N }` using null for a locked
slot. Add the same body's Original Cap column to caps.json -> overrides.entries under the SAME KEY.
The loader checks that originalCap + sum(slots) === newCap and errors if a row was mis-read.

verification.source: NBA 2K HQ app MyPLAYER builder Cap Breaker page (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6745190566), screenshots supplied 2026-08-25.
verification.notes: The five-slot structure, the per-attribute variable gains, the diminishing pattern and the locked slots are all read directly off the app. What is NOT known is how many breakers a player can actually apply — see `allocation`.

verification.source: 2K27 builder coverage: cap breaker amounts are not viewable until 99 overall, and applying them does not provide additional badge tokens.

rules.note: grantsBadgeTokens=false is why the optimizer treats cap breakers as a pure post-build overlay: a breaker can push an attribute over a badge threshold but cannot pay for the badge.

$comment: THE ONE THING THE SCREENSHOTS DO NOT SETTLE. The app shows five slots on every attribute row and
a New Cap that assumes all five are filled. Two readings fit that display equally well:
'shared-pool'   — you earn a limited number of breakers and choose where they go. Filling all
five on Free Throw is possible, but costs you every other placement.
'per-attribute' — every attribute's five slots fill independently, so the New Cap column is
reachable everywhere at once.
'per-attribute' would hand the transcribed build +112 attribute points for free, which is a very
large claim to make on the strength of a display that is equally consistent with scarcity. So the
default is 'shared-pool', which is the conservative reading: it can under-promise, never
over-promise. Switch `mode` to 'per-attribute' if the generous reading turns out to be right.
`poolSize` is a guess and is the single least-supported number in this file.

verification.notes: Neither the mode nor the pool size is sourced. The GAIN TABLE is verified; how many of those gains you may claim is not.

eligibility.note: mode may be 'all', 'all-except' (uses excludedAttributes) or 'only' (uses includedAttributes). Per-attribute lock-out is expressed by null slots in the gain table, not here.

$comment: Keyed exactly like caps.json -> overrides.entries: `<POSITION>|<height>|<weight>|<wingspan>`,
with `*` matching anything and the most specific match winning.
A body with no matching entry gets no cap breaker plan. That is deliberate: gains vary so wildly
between attributes on the one body we have that interpolating to another body would be fiction.

PF|83|210|83.label: 6'11" / 210 lb / 6'11" PF — shown in the NBA 2K HQ builder as BUCKET CHASER
